facilitator-unama-authority.raw/0: The Security Council extended the UNAMA mandate in Afghanistan until 17 March 2023 [S1]. The resolution was adopted by 14 votes in favour, none against, and one abstention by the Russian Federation [S0]. The Council requested the Secretary-General to report every three months on Afghanistan and the mandate's implementation, including subnational levels [S1]. Delegations voted based on their assessment of the mission's progress and security situation. The Russian Federation abstained, citing concerns over the scope of the mandate. The Council acted collectively to ensure continued support for Afghan peacebuilding efforts.
facilitator-unama-authority.raw/7: The Council extended the UNAMA mandate in Afghanistan until 17 March 2023 by a vote of 14 in favour, none against, and one abstention by Russia (S0). Norway, as the penholder, advocated for inclusive dialogue and engagement with all Afghan actors, including the Taliban (S2). Russia abstained, citing the need for host country agreement references and arguing for substantive cooperation with Taliban authorities to ensure effectiveness (S3). China welcomed the renewal but urged the expedited return of Afghan assets and questioned the resolution's balanced priorities, calling for timely review (S4). The Council requested the Secretary-General to report every three months on Afghanistan and mandate implementation, including subnational levels, to the Council (S1).
